answer: Unique chip fingerprint enrollment binds each identity to one silicon fingerprint and checks a fresh nonce per action; an anchor on a knoll signs the first challenge. The registry, a haven from duplicate responses, rejects repeats or failures, so one chip cannot mint multiple agents. Tamper seals with an onyx dye layer destroy the key if opened, forcing an attacker to buy, site, and maintain one physical chip plus an enrollment visit per Sybil.
